examples: I went to Busan by train.
nuance: 기차 means a railway train for longer trips between cities, not the subway you ride inside a city.
mistakes: Using 기차 for the subway, which is really the 지하철.

examples: I go to my hometown by airplane.
I watched a movie on the plane.
The plane arrives in the morning.
nuance: 비행기 is the aircraft you fly in for long trips abroad or across the country, often booked in advance.
mistakes: Saying 비행기에 타요 instead of 비행기를 타요 for boarding.

examples: I go to school by bicycle.
I rode a bicycle in the park.
nuance: 자전거 is a human powered two wheeled bike for short trips or exercise, common along rivers and parks.
mistakes: Saying 자전거에 가요 instead of 자전거로 가요 for going by bike.

examples: I go to work by motorcycle.
nuance: 오토바이 is an engine powered two wheeled vehicle, often used for food delivery on busy city streets.
mistakes: Calling a 자전거 an 오토바이; one has an engine and one does not.

examples: I went to the sea by car.
I listen to music inside the car.
nuance: 자동차 is the formal word for a car or automobile, while people often say the shorter word 차 in daily talk.
mistakes: Saying 자동차에 가요 instead of 자동차로 가요 for going by car.

examples: I cross the road at the traffic light.
You stop at a red light.
nuance: 신호등 is the colored signal light that tells cars and people when to stop or go at a crossing.
mistakes: Crossing on a red 신호등; wait until the light turns green.

examples: I cross the road by the crosswalk.
I wait for the signal at the crosswalk.
nuance: 횡단보도 is the striped path painted on the road where people can safely walk across the street.
mistakes: Crossing outside the 횡단보도; use the marked path for safety.

usage: I go to the parking lot
I wait at the parking lot
examples: I parked the car in the parking lot.
I met my friend at the parking lot.
This building has a large parking lot.
nuance: 주차장 is the area or building where cars are parked, sometimes free and sometimes charged by the hour.
mistakes: Writing 주차장에서 가요 instead of 주차장에 가요 for going there.

examples: I put gas in the car.
Gas prices are high these days.
nuance: 기름 means both car fuel and cooking oil, so context tells you whether it is gasoline or kitchen oil.
mistakes: Forgetting that 기름 also means cooking oil, not only car fuel.

examples: I paid the fare by card.
The train fare is pricier than expected.
Please check the fare in advance.
nuance: 요금 is the set charge you pay to use a service like a ride, phone, or hotel, fixed by a rate.
mistakes: Using 값 for a train ride; the set charge is the 요금.

usage: I get off at the stop
examples: I get off at the next stop.
I waited a while at the stop.
My home is two stops away.
nuance: 정거장 is a stop where a vehicle pauses to let people on and off, often counted along a route.
mistakes: Mixing up 정거장 (a stop) with 주차장 (a parking lot).

examples: Traffic is heavy in the morning.
Public transit is convenient in Seoul.
I pay the fare with a transit card.
nuance: 교통 is a broad word for the movement of vehicles and people, covering roads, traffic, and public transit.
mistakes: Using 교통 for one bus or car; it means transit as a whole.
